How to Tell If Your Bra Fits Correctly — 5 Signs to Check

The 5 evidence-based checks that distinguish a well-fitting bra from an ill-fitting one. Spot poor fit instantly with this guide.

The 5-Sign Fit Test

You do not need a mirror, a fitter, or a tape measure to know whether a bra fits. The following five checks, developed by professional bra fitters and validated in sports-medicine research [1] , take about 30 seconds. If any of these fail, the bra is the wrong size, the wrong shape, or both.

1. The Band Test (Most Important)

The band carries about 80–90% of breast weight . A proper band should be snug on the loosest hook when the bra is new (tighten as the elastic relaxes). If the band rides up the back, the bra is too big in the band — or the straps are doing too much work.

Quick test: Run two fingers under the band at the back. They should slide in snugly with a bit of resistance.

2. The Underwire Test

The underwire (if present) should lie flat against the chest wall, with the wire's curve following your breast root. The wire must not dig into breast tissue, rest on breast tissue, or sit on the armpit.

Common error: Wearing a cup that is too small pushes the wire onto breast tissue instead of around it. This is both uncomfortable and biomechanically wrong.

3. The Spillage Test

Lean forward 45 degrees and look in a mirror. All breast tissue should sit inside the cup, with no spillage at the top, sides, or center gore. If you see "bra bulge" above the cup line, the cup is too small.

4. The Strap Test

Straps should be tight enough to stay in place but not dig into the shoulders. You should be able to fit one or two fingers under each strap. If the straps are sliding off, the band is too loose; if they are leaving red marks, they are overcompensating for a too-loose band.

5. The Gore Test

The center gore (the small piece of fabric between the cups) should lie flat against the sternum. If it bows out or floats away from your chest, the cup size is too small.

Visual Fit Comparison

The following table summarizes the visible signs of common fit problems:

Fit Problem Visible Sign Likely Cause
Band rides up Back of band higher than front Band too big; tighten hooks or go down a band size
Quad-boob (top spillage) Tissue bulges over cup top Cup too small; go up a cup size
Underwire on breast tissue Wire presses into underarm or breast Cup too small or wrong shape; try a different style
Gaps in cup Empty space in upper cup Cup too big or wrong shape (full-on-bottom breast with shallow cup)
Straps dig in Shoulder indentations or pain Band too loose; straps overcompensating
Straps fall off Straps slide down the arm Band too big or narrow shoulders; try racer-back style

Why This Matters

An ill-fitting bra contributes to shoulder grooving, back pain, skin irritation, and reduced breast support during exercise [2] . The good news is that a properly fitted bra is one of the most cost-effective ways to improve daily comfort, posture, and confidence [3] .

FAQs

What if I am between two band sizes?

Choose the smaller band and a larger cup. For example, if you measure 31 inches, go with a 32 band and a +1 cup size. The smaller band gives better support and is easier to adjust with the hooks as the elastic wears.

Should I fit a new bra on the loosest or tightest hook?

New bras should fit on the loosest hook. As the elastic relaxes over 3–6 months, you move to the middle hook, then the tightest. This extends the bra's useful life by 2–3 months.

Is wireless better than underwire?

Both can fit well. Underwire provides more lift and projection, especially for D+ cup sizes, but only if the wire fits the breast root. Wireless bras are often more comfortable for smaller cup sizes, lounging, and post-surgery.
